one_line: Cheap on fear of AI agents, a US fee probe and slowing travel. The -1% sales figure is a one-off charge; real growth is about +9%. Slowdown is real.

why_fell.reason: Fear that AI travel agents and Google cut out booking sites
why_fell.evidence: Morgan Stanley test sent AI searches to hotel sites 97% of the time. Booking says AI referrals are still well under 1% of room nights.

why_fell.reason: US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) matter on Priceline
why_fell.evidence: Q3 took a $900M revenue cut and $100M loss accrual. No settlement yet; penalties could exceed $1B per reports.

why_fell.reason: Travel demand cooled late in Q3 and Q4 guidance is weak
why_fell.evidence: Q4 room nights guided up 1-3%, adjusted revenue up 0-2%, adjusted EBITDA about flat. Middle East conflict and European unrest hurt October.

why_fell.reason: Lower valuation, not lower profit estimates
why_fell.evidence: Forward price-to-earnings about 14x versus a five-year average near 21x, while consensus earnings keep rising.

for_unfair.point: Your -1% sales figure is distorted. Reported revenue $8.9B fell 1% only because of the $900M FTC cut. Excluding it, adjusted revenue was $9.8B, up 9% (10% at constant currency).
Volume is healthy: room nights 345M, up 7%; gross bookings $54.5B, up 10% (11% constant currency). Adjusted EPS $4.66 beat the $4.50 estimate, up 17%.
Google's AI Mode hotel booking launched with Booking.com and Priceline as launch partners, so far routing bookings through them. Four of five recent analyst calls say Buy.

for_fair.point: Growth is slowing fast: Q3 room nights +7% but Q4 guided +1-3%, and bookings +2-4% reported. Management shelved a margin target, per one report.
The FTC cost is real money, not just accounting: $1B booked, possibly more, and a separate San Francisco suit plus a European Commission probe on practices.
AI risk is early but credible: Morgan Stanley says agents steer travelers to direct hotel sites. Analysts have cut targets (Goldman $180, Cantor $150, Wells $190).

what_market_fears: AI agents and Google let hotels sell direct, shrinking Booking's fees. Add a growing US fee case, EU rules, and a travel slowdown.
what_would_prove_it_wrong: Q4 room nights near or above the 1-3% guide, AI referrals staying under 1% of nights, FTC settling near the $1B already booked.
next_date_to_watch: Q4 2026 results, expected February 2027 (date not confirmed); any FTC settlement news before then.

flag.note: Not tripped: AI referrals under 1% of room nights. Google's tool lists Booking as partner. But Morgan Stanley test shows agents favor hotel sites; early only.

not_found: Stock split: 25-for-1, effective April 2026, so no change in value (release says April 2; one report says trading from April 6). EU: no fine found; Sept 2026 the Commission said Booking removed price-parity rules under the Digital Markets Act (source: digital-markets-act.ec.europa.eu factsheet, 2026-09-28, summary only); a separate EU probe and Greek case remain. Current price of $146.64 and 33% drop not independently verified; stock closed $155.67 Nov 3 and one report says it rose about 10% after earnings. Analyst page from Benzinga could not be fetched. Google's own effect on bookings: not found.
